## Why We Are Starting With the Doubling Cube

We are starting with the doubling cube because it is one of the hardest parts of backgammon to learn by intuition alone.

Checker play gives you multipe options to choose from.  The cube changes the value of the game with only 2 options. You must decide whether your advantage is large enough to double or just roll on.  Receivers decide if they should take or pass.

These choices become easier when they are broken into smaller questions. That is what the first learning path will do.

::: {.callout-note}
The doubling cube is only the beginning. Lessons on checker play, openings, match play, endgames, and engine analysis are coming soon.
:::

## More Lessons Are Coming

The full Learn section will grow to include:

| Track | What you will learn |
|---|---|
| **Start Here** | How to read the board, follow lesson positions, and understand common terms |
| **Checker Play** | Racing, safety, flexibility, timing, contact, and tactical choices |
| **Opening Play** | Early moves, replies, and how game plans begin |
| **Match Play** | How the score changes checker and cube decisions |
| **Endgames** | Bearoffs, wastage, racing, timing, and practical counting |
| **Engines and Analysis** | How to understand evaluations, equity, error rates, and rollouts |

Beginners will be able to follow each path from the start. More experienced players can move directly to the questions they want to study.
